title: GUILTY, THOUGH WE DID NOT KNOW

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If anyone sins and does what is forbidden in any of the LORD's commands, even though they do not know it, they are guilty and will be held responsible.'" - Lev 5:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse is difficult, and it is meant to be. They do not know it. They are guilty. Both statements stand.

We instinctively resist this. Surely guilt requires awareness? Surely I cannot be held responsible for a rule I never knew existed?

But think about how this works in ordinary life. A driver who did not see the speed limit sign has still broken the law. A man who did not realise he was hurting his wife has still hurt her. Ignorance explains; it does not undo.

The reason this matters spiritually is that it destroys a comfortable illusion — the idea that I am basically fine because I cannot think of anything serious I have done. Leviticus says your knowledge of your own condition is not the measure of your condition.

Paul reached the same conclusion: I am not aware of anything against myself, but I am not thereby acquitted (1 Cor 4:4). Jeremiah put it more starkly: the heart is deceitful above all things (Jer 17:9).

This is not designed to crush us. It is designed to drive us away from self-assessment and toward Christ, whose blood covers what we can name and what we cannot. That is a far safer place to stand than on the flimsy foundation of a clear conscience.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I measure my standing before God by what I happen to be aware of?
2. Does my assurance rest on my own record or on Christ's work?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I cannot see myself clearly, and I am glad my hope does not depend on it. Thank You that Christ covers even the sins I do not know I have. Amen.
